findings.text: the obligation map is rewritten whole on every pass from only the plans that pass weighed, so a held plan the one-plan pass limit or the rotation does not reach loses the reason recorded for it on the previous pass, and the owner's obligations view then shows a review owed with no reason while the plan still holds its request

_plan_review_holds re-implements the held-request predicate (phase held, an automatic hold, reason plan-review-owed, plan via _run_plan) that obligations.py:5439-5452 already applies, adding a second copy of one rule rather than extracting the owner both read

for a held plan _held_plan_obligation calls review_coverage and compose_burst_refusal again after _owed_review_skip_reason (plan_review.py:4890-4902) already computed both, so each held plan costs a second and often third store walk in one pass, the read amplification test_a_pass_computes_coverage_once measures

the assertion compares the stamp the test itself passed to _record_weighed_edits through _weigh_at_current_edit against the same path.stat().st_mtime, so it holds even if the pass stopped calling _record_weighed_edits at all; the assertions that do redden on that regression are report['read'] == [] and launched == [] at lines 178-180
